headline: Learning to Navigate Cancer Care
lede: A diagnosis opens a second, less visible ordeal: coordinating specialists, records, tests, and decisions. One patient’s account is a practical case for persistence, careful documentation, and informed skepticism about easy answers—including those offered by AI.

headline: The Router That Needed Root Access
lede: A cache-coherency bug corrupted packets while reporting valid checksums. With the vendor gone and the offload switch unavailable, a known kernel exploit became the unlikely repair tool.

headline: OpenCode Rebuilds Its Core
lede: OpenCode 2.0 turns a persistent local service into the center of its TUI, web, desktop, and CLI clients. Hot-reloadable plugins, asynchronous agents, and a new SDK arrive with a hard break from the 1.0 server API.

headline: A Tiny Office Fits in the Browser
lede: Word processing, spreadsheets, diagrams, calendars, and more arrive as one linkable web suite. Tiny Little Office favors breadth and low friction over the ceremony of a conventional productivity stack.

headline: Plant Advice, Plotted by Place
lede: Indigene turns location, light, soil, and garden goals into native-plant suggestions. It runs offline, asks for no account, and documents the open data and cautious AI-assisted process behind the recommendations.

headline: When Every Dentist Has a Different Answer
lede: A patient’s jaw becomes a tour through contradictory diagnoses, escalating procedures, and uncertain evidence. The essay argues for conservative care and independent judgment when expertise and incentives point in several directions.
pullquote: A treatment plan should not become more certain merely because it becomes more expensive.

headline: A 24-Billion-Parameter Model Goes Local
lede: Liquid AI’s mixture-of-experts model activates only a small fraction of its total weights per token, targeting fast private agents on consumer hardware. Its long context, tool-use training, and broad runtime support make the practical test speed plus judgment—not parameter count alone.

headline: The Broadcast Network of Rural Argentina
lede: Since the 1930s and 1940s, Patagonia’s radio hosts have carried news of illness, travel, animals, and family across immense distances. Satellite links may be arriving, but the daily broadcast remains both infrastructure and companionship.

headline: A Tree Grows From Good News
lede: Catch a Bird turns one-sentence happiness into birds on a shared virtual tree. There are no accounts to manage and little to optimize—just an ephemeral, gently moderated garden of things strangers wanted to remember.

headline: Thirty Years of Losing the Room
lede: A new survey comparison finds marked declines in many forms of in-person American social activity, from club meetings to volunteering. The trend is substantial but not exact: differing samples and methods make the historical contrast suggestive rather than definitive.
